target: Prospective v2 complete CSharp source policy; every expected rejection preserves existing API/namespace/identifier restrictions.
expected_result_scope: Complete policy acceptance, not just a substring search. Literal/comment words are inert, interpolation expressions remain executable, and identifier canonical ValueText cannot bypass existing bans.
execution_policy: Defensive validator fixtures only. Never compile-and-run these programs; lexical/syntax policy inspection does not execute them.
csharp_language: CSharp 11 or later for raw and UTF8 literals. All sources are intended as complete syntactically valid programs with Main(string[] args).

cases.criterion: API names inside ordinary string text are not executable identifiers.
Reject an actual fully qualified Process.Start call.
Reject construction of an actual Process object.
Preserve both alias/global:: restrictions and the underlying Process ban.
Verbatim string quoting must hide only literal text, including doubled quotes.
Raw string content containing quotes and API words remains inert text.
The UTF8 literal suffix does not turn API words into identifiers.
Ignore interpolated text while retaining the safe args.Length expression.
An interpolation expression is executable code; do not erase its Environment call with the enclosing string.
Double-dollar raw interpolation expressions retain actual API identifiers.
Recursively retain an API expression inside a raw interpolated string nested in another raw interpolation.
UTF16 span conversion must still mask a harmless literal after an astral character.
An astral character before a masked literal must not shift masking over a subsequent real API call.
CSharp identifier ValueText is Process; preserve escaped-identifier and actual API restrictions.
The @ prefix does not hide canonical Process; preserve verbatim-identifier restrictions.
Preserve the current qualified System.Func restriction outside literal text.
Preserve the actual StreamReader restriction outside literal text.
Line and block comments containing forbidden API words are inert and must not cause API rejection.
